# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Age:** Young adult  <sub>[v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher at Pale Sands school  <sub>[v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal was a striking young woman with fair skin, light blue eyes, and long yellow hair worn in braids. Her looks possessed a vivid, bold charm that made her stand out alongside her peers. During her final illness, her face grew pale, childlike, and delicate, retaining its beauty even after her death.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P16](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0016), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Personality

Opal had a merry, cheerful, and lighthearted disposition, often engrossed in social life, bright clothing, and talk of her suitors. Beneath her optimistic and optimistic exterior lay a worldly nature focused on simple earthly pleasures. Facing her terminal illness, she harbored a deep fear of death and the unfamiliarity of the afterlife, longing earnestly to live a normal life with love and a family.

_Sources: [v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P14](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0014), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P19](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0019)_

## Traits

- Cheerful and optimistic  <sub>[v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002)</sub>
- Feminine and fond of fine clothing  <sub>[v3 c11 P52](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0052), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053)</sub>
- Fond of babies and children  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
- Fear of dying and the unknown afterlife  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P19](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Fancy needlework and embroidery  <sub>[v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P33](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0033)</sub>

## Goals

- To live, get married, and raise children  <sub>[v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>

## History

During her youth in Brierley, Opal spent midsummer afternoons playing outdoor games with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen around the local pond. She later took up a teaching position at Pale Sands school, though her declining health forced her to step down before completing her term. As her illness worsened, she spent her final summer resting in her garden, frequently seeking the companionship of Nell, in whom she eventually confided her fear of death and her unfulfilled wish to marry Herb Tranter and raise a family. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in the local graveyard near her family home, leaving an unfinished piece of embroidery to Nell.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c14 P0](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0000), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P32](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0032), [v3 c14 P33](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Attended school alongside Nell, Isolde, and Emma White  <sub>[v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023)</sub>
- Suffered from chest congestion during a previous winter  <sub>[v3 c11 P57](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0057)</sub>

## Quotes

> Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Will you come up frequently, Nell? Make sure to come by yourself—I need you.  <sub>[v3 c11 P55](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0055)</sub>

> Nell, the time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. I ponder—and ponder—and it makes me so scared—and—and—homesick.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
